newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: U.S., allies issue Dayton ultimatum to Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S., allies issue Dayton ultimatum to Bosnia.

text.p: The United States and the western allies, fearing Bosnia's peace is in danger of unravelling, told the former warring parties on Friday to implement the Dayton peace accords in full or face a number of sanctions.

In their toughest statement since Dayton was signed 18 months ago, the big powers detailed measures, including denying visas to people who have contacts with indicted war criminals, if Bosnia's Moslems, Croats and Serbs did not stick to the deal.

A copy of the final communique of a meeting of the Peace Implementation Council, created by Dayton, ordered Bosnia's elected authorities to take the necessary action to reform property laws, pass citizenship laws, restructure police forces, and hand over indicted war criminals.

The U.S., France, and Britain, the main contributors to an international peace force in the country, fear failure to make progress in implementing the civilian aspects of Dayton could see Bosnia slip back into war after its mandate expires next July or force them to keep troops there indefinitely.

The communique said if the new three-man Bosnian presidency had not appointed new ambassadors by August 1 this year to represent the entire country then all contact with existing missions would be broken off.

From January 1998, the allies said only cars with new Bosnian registration plates would be allowed across international frontiers and warned existing nationalist flags and other symbols would no longer be recognised after September 1 this year.

The allies also said people dealing with indicted war criminals, such as former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic, could have the right to travel abroad withdrawn. Economic aid would be cut off to "those municipalities which continue to tolerate indicted persons working in a public capacity."
